h: פָּרָשַׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ, מַאֲמָר א׳ Parshas HaChodesh — Maamar Aleph

p: On the fourth Shabbos we read
and it is called Parshas HaChodesh,
just as Parshas Shekalim is so called
and not called Parshas Ki Sisa,
which is not called Parshas Chukas HaTorah,
so too it ought to have called
Rather, the main intent of the parshah
is what it says, "This month shall be for you,"
which is the beginning of words of Torah,
as they said: Rabbi Yitzchak said,
לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְהַתְחִיל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
"The Torah should not have needed to begin
except from 'This month shall be for you,'
which is the first mitzvah" etc.
(as Rashi writes at the beginning of Parshas Bereishis);
and so it is brought in the holy Zohar
"The Torah need not have been written
except from 'This month shall be for you' etc.
Because it is the beginning of the moon.
should have been written from here,
for with the Holy One, blessed be He,
that it does not say 'zos hachodesh,' 'hazos,'
are bound together as one" etc.
The point is that the moon
and the Shechinah is the aspect of the moon
And here is the beginning of recognition,
that there is a light that is recognized,
and one can point to it with a finger: "This."
And this is "for it is the beginning of the moon."
And the Torah should have begun there,
"for it is bound up with the Holy One, blessed be He" —
"And we have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He,
and there is no Torah but
the Holy One, blessed be He.
And here the first mitzvah was given to Yisrael:
to bring holiness into the month,
when it is filled from the holy,
And it says, "for zeh and zos
comes from the side of the Holy One, blessed be He,
"Since you have been sanctified to My Name" etc.,
just as I am holy" etc.;
"A parable — to what may this be compared?" etc.:
"I am king and you are queen" etc.
And this is what they said, "for zeh and zos
And this is a preface to the mitzvah of the Pesach offering,
for the descendants of Noach have no power
to eat an eating in holiness,
"The descendants of Noach did not offer shelamim."
And even according to the view that they did offer shelamim,
nonetheless regarding the Pesach it is explicit:
כָּל בֶּן נֵכָר לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ
וְכָל עָרֵל לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ [שְׁמוֹת יב, מח]
and "no uncircumcised man shall eat of it" (Shemos 12:48).
And after they were given Parshas HaChodesh,
through which they became the Jewish nation,
then they were given the mitzvah of the Pesach.
And it says, "for zeh and zos
and in a place where male and female are together,
the praise goes only to the male;
and therefore: 'It is first for you
of the months of the year.'"
For "year" refers to the solar year,
at the completion of the cycle,
and the sun is exactly as it was at first;
at the birth of the moon,
and the next day her belly is between her teeth" etc.;
new light from the light of the sun,
and this is its being born anew.
And when it says "of the months of the year,"
the renewal of the moon, as mentioned above,
which repeats every year, as mentioned above;
Why does it say 'for you' twice?
'For Hashem's portion is His people'" etc.
And this follows what they said
"'And they shall take for Me' etc. —
as it were, I was sold along with it" etc.
That is, they became Hashem's portion,
for the holiness of Hashem Yisbarach is not recognized
except through the holiness of Yisrael,
who receive from the holiness of Hashem Yisbarach.
(And it was explained in Yisro, maamar 7.)
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר לָכֶם תְּרֵי זִמְנֵי
And on this it says "for you" twice:
And it says, "This bond is 'for you'
and not for the other nations,"
along the lines of what they said
and the matron sits opposite him;
"'And they shall take for themselves, each man' (Shemos 12:3) —
this is the Holy One, blessed be He,
That is, through the mitzvah of the Pesach
the mitzvah of the Pesach could not apply to Yisrael
to the holiness of Hashem Yisbarach
and could eat an eating in holiness.
the mitzvah of "This month shall be for you"
for He gave them the power
to bring holiness into the month;
and afterward the mitzvah of the Pesach was given
and can eat an eating in holiness.
And this is what we learned (Rosh Hashanah 24a):
"The head of the beis din says, 'Sanctified,'
and all the people answer after him,
דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁאָמַר רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין מְקוּדָּשׁ
For once the head of the beis din said "Sanctified,"
all Yisrael then had the power
to bring holiness into the month.
וְאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ בְּאוֹתוֹ פָּרָשָׁה [שָׁם, טז]
And afterward it says in that same parshah (ibid. 12:16):
"And on the first day, a holy convocation,
and on the seventh day, a holy convocation."
they can bring holiness into time.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר לָהֶם [שָׁם יג, ט-טז]
which is a crown upon the head.
And although the main revelation of Atika
they merited at the splitting of the Yam Suf,
since already at the plague of the firstborn
נִקְרְאוּ בְּנִי בְכוֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל [שָׁם ד, כב]
they were called "My son, My firstborn, Yisrael" (ibid. 4:22),
meaning that they are bound to the beginning of Thought —
the parshah of tefillin was told to them.
And on Shabbos, which is itself a sign,
it is not a time for tefillin (Eruvin 96a),
for then all Yisrael are bound to the root,
and they are like those who go about all day in tefillin
(and it was explained in Pekudei, maamar 9).

paragraphs.text: Rashi, Bereishis 1:1 — “Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Torah should have begun only with This month shall be for you, which is the first commandment commanded to Israel. Why did it begin with Bereishis? Because He declared to His people the power of His works, to give them the inheritance of nations. If the nations tell Israel, You are robbers, for you conquered the lands of the seven nations, Israel answer: The whole earth belongs to the Holy One, blessed be He. He created it and gave it to whomever He saw fit.” Rashi speaks of the first commandment addressed to Israel. Rav Tzadok develops its significance as the beginning of Israel's participation in sanctifying time.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 39b, Bo 7, s.v. Amar Rabbi Yitzchak — “Rabbi Yitzchak said: Torah needed to be written only from This month shall be for you, the head of months. Why? Because it was the moon's beginning; Torah should have begun here because the matter is bound to the Holy One, blessed be He. There is no difficulty that it does not say this in the feminine, for the masculine this and feminine this are bound together. Where male and female are together, praise is assigned to the male; therefore, It is first for you, for the months of the year. Rabbi Yehudah asked: Why for you twice? Rabbi Yitzchak answered: More is heard through them, as it is written, For Hashem's portion is His people. This bond is for you, not for the other nations.” The original passage contains both questions developed in the discourse: the masculine demonstrative and the repeated for you. Rav Tzadok explains both through the union of Divine bestowal and Israel's reception of holiness.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Beis Yaakov (Izhbitz), Bereishis 8 — on the Zohar’s “because it is the beginning of the moon”: “This means that there the true intent of creation begins to be revealed, since human sanctification and the mitzvos start at that point.” The Izhbitzer’s son reads the Zohar the same way. The Torah “should have begun” here because this is where Yisrael first bring holiness into creation themselves.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 15:24 — “If an ordinary vessel becomes sanctified when filled with something holy, how much more Israel, who are holy and sanctify the month. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am holy; do I sanctify only Myself? Rather, I sanctify Israel, and they sanctify Me. Therefore it is written, You shall be holy to Me, and, For I, Hashem, who sanctifies you, am holy.” The Midrash explicitly joins Israel's received holiness with their ability to sanctify the month. Rav Tzadok reads this as the union of the giver of light and its recipient.

paragraphs.text: Zevachim 116a — “Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina disagreed: one said that the descendants of Noach offered peace-offerings, and one said that they did not. What is the reason of the one who says they did not? Awake, north, and come, south: the nation whose service is in the north should move aside, and the nation whose service is in both north and south should come.” The Gemara preserves both views. Rav Tzadok expressly argues that even the view allowing peace-offerings does not overcome the Passover offering's explicit restrictions.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 25a — “Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas said: They are false witnesses. How can they testify concerning a woman that she gave birth, while on the following day her belly is between her teeth? Rabbi Yehoshua told him: I see the force of your words.” The comparison concerns testimony to the new moon followed by the appearance of the old moon. Rav Tzadok takes its language of birth as an image of the moon's renewed light.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 33:1 — “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: I sold you My Torah; as it were, I was sold with it. ... This is compared to a king with an only daughter. Another king married her and wished to take her to his land. Her father said: I cannot part from her, and I cannot tell you not to take her, since she is your wife. Do me this kindness: wherever you go, make me a little chamber, so that I may dwell with you. ... So the Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Wherever you go, make Me one house in which to dwell, as it is said, They shall make Me a sanctuary.” The Midrash interprets taking a contribution for Me through God's inseparability from His Torah. Rav Tzadok links that attachment with the doubled for you in the commandment of the month.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Zohar II 186a (Tetzaveh) — “‘This month is for you’: it is Mine, but I have handed it over to you; yours is in revelation, but the seventh is Mine, and so it is covered and not revealed.” The Zohar supports Rav Tzadok’s reading of the double “for you.” Hashem, the First, gives Himself over to Yisrael through Nisan, the month of revelation.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 25:11 — “What is meant by He gave to you? It was given to you, not to the nations. ... It says, Between Me and the children of Israel. This is compared to a king seated with the queen seated opposite him: whoever passes between them is liable.” The original context is Shabbos as a covenant between God and Israel. Rav Tzadok borrows its image to explain the distinctive bond expressed by for you in HaChodesh.

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbasi 15:24, HaChodesh — “They shall take for themselves a man: this is the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is written, Hashem is a man of war, whom you take through the two continual offerings. A lamb: this is the continual offering, as it says, The one lamb you shall offer in the morning.” The Midrash's immediate explanation is the two tamid offerings. Rav Tzadok extends its language of taking God to the Passover commandment in the surrounding section.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 24a — “The head of the court says: Sanctified! All the people answer after him: Sanctified, sanctified! ... From where is it learned that all the people answer after him? Rav Pappa said: Scripture says, Which you shall proclaim them; read it as you. ... Why twice, Sanctified, sanctified? Because it is written, Holy convocations. Whether it was seen at its expected time or was not seen at its expected time, they sanctify it.” The Mishnah and Gemara include the people in the proclamation. Rav Tzadok reads their response as participation in the holiness conferred by the court.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 96a — “Rabbi Akiva says: Could a person put on tefillin on Shabbosos and festivals? Scripture says, It shall be for you a sign upon your hand: those that require a sign. These are excluded, for they themselves are a sign.” Rav Tzadok explains the festival itself as an embodied sign of holiness, corresponding to the holiness expressed by tefillin.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kedoshim 8 — “At Matan Torah each of Yisrael was crowned with the two crowns… and though they later removed them, Pri Etz Chaim says that on Shabbos Moshe Rabbeinu returns the crowns to Yisrael.” This gives the Arizal’s reason why Shabbos needs no tefillin. The crowns that tefillin restore are already given back on Shabbos.
